hints.title: 8-Directional Pathfinding Obstacle
hints.text: Moving diagonally and cardinally across an N x N binary grid from top-left to bottom-right requires finding the fewest steps without visiting blocked 1 cells. How can level-order progression find the shortest clear path?

hints.title: Clear Cell 8-Way Wave Invariant
hints.text: Because every step between 8-directionally adjacent cells has identical edge weight 1, the first time the bottom-right corner is dequeued, the path length is minimal.

hints.title: Layered Traversal Procedure
hints.text: If start cell or target cell is non-zero, return -1. If n == 1, return 1. Enqueue (0, 0, 1) and mark grid[0][0] = 1. While queue is not empty, pop (r, c, d). Check all 8 directions. If (nr, nc) is (n-1, n-1), return d + 1. If valid and grid[nr][nc] == 0, mark grid[nr][nc] = 1 and enqueue (nr, nc, d + 1). Return -1 if exhausted.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every cell is processed at most once across 8 directions in O(N^2) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Depth search explores exponentially many non-optimal paths before reaching the target.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place grid cell marking avoids allocating separate visited structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling corner cases where start or end cells are blocked with 1.
